title: Composite Fermion Theory of Fractional Chern Insulators in Rhombohedral Graphene
authors: Peize Ding, Andrew J. Millis, Yongxin Zeng
abstract: The experimental observation of the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect in rhombohedral graphene multilayers has raised questions about the nature of the fractional Chern insulator (FCI) states and the role of the moiré potential. In this Letter we develop a composite fermion (CF) description and discuss how moiré modulation and Coulomb interactions stabilize the FCI ground states. Under a flux-attachment transformation and mean-field approximation, the CF spectrum forms Landau levels that are further split by the moiré potential. At moiré filling fractions in the Jain sequence, an integer number of CF bands are occupied, resulting in an incompressible ground state with fractionally quantized Hall response. Remarkably, when the attached flux opposes the Berry curvature of the conduction band of rhombohedral graphene, the CF Landau levels are widely spaced in energy and delocalized across layers, leading to a reduced density of states that helps protect the CF mean-field state and amplifying effects of the moiré potential acting on the layer away from the doped electrons. Interactions between CFs further enlarge the moiré-induced band gap and stabilize the FCI ground state. Our work sheds light on the nature of the FCI states in rhombohedral graphene and provides a new theoretical framework for further studies.
summary: This work develops a Composite Fermion theory to explain Fractional Chern Insulators in rhombohedral graphene. By incorporating moiré modulation and Coulomb interactions via a mean-field approach, the authors show how these effects stabilize the FCI ground state. The theory predicts quantized Hall responses characteristic of these topological phases.
main_problem: The paper investigates the nature of Fractional Chern Insulator (FCI) states in rhombohedral graphene (RLG) and how the moiré potential and Coulomb interactions stabilize these exotic quantum states.
main_result: The composite fermion (CF) theory successfully describes the FCI ground state, predicting fractionally quantized Hall responses when the system is at Jain sequence filling fractions.
method: The primary theoretical tool is the Composite Fermion (CF) theory, utilizing a flux-attachment transformation and subsequent mean-field (Hartree-Fock) approximation to treat electron-electron interactions.
model_or_system: The system is rhombohedral graphene multilayers (RLG) subjected to moiré modulation and electron-electron Coulomb interactions. The Hamiltonian is analyzed using a continuum model framework adapted for the moiré superlattice.
key_observables: Fractionally quantized Hall conductance ($\sigma_{xy}$), the CF energy spectrum (Landau Levels split by moiré potential), and the Chern number ($C$).
important_parameters:
Moiré filling fractions (Jain sequence, e.g., $
u=1/3$), the attached magnetic flux quanta ($2s$), and the moiré potential strength ($\phi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the CF mean-field approximation, treating the moiré potential phenomenologically, and assuming spin/valley polarization for simplification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the CF theory progression: flux attachment leading to LLs split by the moiré potential into sub-bands (Jain sequence example). Other figures show band structures, layer polarization, and density distributions under different interaction regimes.
paper_structure: The paper develops the CF framework, applies mean-field theory to incorporate moiré and interaction effects, calculates the resulting topological invariants (Chern numbers), and predicts the incompressible ground state characteristic of FCIs.
why_interesting: The theoretical framework of CFs and the explicit inclusion of moiré potentials to stabilize topological phases are highly relevant to understanding strongly correlated electron systems in engineered 2D materials.
